card.name: Rouf
card.tagline: Kashmiri women's spring and Eid line dance
card.profile: Rouf (pronounced 'ruf' in villages, 'row' in towns; also Rouff) is a Kashmiri women's folk dance that welcomes spring and is also performed during Eid and Ramzan (J&K Tourism). Dancers form two parallel rows facing each other with interlocked or held hands, swaying forward and backward; its hallmark is intricate synchronised footwork (J&K Tourism). It originated within the Muslim community of the Kashmir Valley and was later embraced across the valley; women wear colourful pheran with a headscarf and traditional silver jewellery (J&K Tourism; INTACH).
card.insight: Rouf is performed communally on joyous occasions and traditionally marks the arrival of spring, embodying the seasonal rhythm of the valley; songs accompanying it are often interwoven with the chakri musical tradition (INTACH; Music of Jammu and Kashmir).
